title: Session-driven recorders must seed state before flushSync mounts, share the overlay's video finder, and re-anchor on boundary states (past-last-range / ended) instead of finalizing before any capture
trigger: a pill/overlay flashes then disappears right after session start, or NaN shows in elapsed counters, especially on pages with multiple <video> elements (YouTube mixes, previews)
problem: Condensed-audio record on YouTube mounted the pill showing NaN:NaN then vanished without recording. Three compounding root causes: (1) mountCondensedAudioPill ran flushSync render BEFORE Object.assign populated the session, so getElapsedMs() read undefined → formatElapsed(undefined) → 'NaN:NaN'; (2) the recorder picked its own video via querySelectorAll + longest-duration sort while the subtitle overlay picked via findLargestPlayableVideo (visible, shadow-piercing) — on multi-video pages they diverged, so cues/ranges and playback targeted different elements; (3) any boundary state reached with capturedMs===0 (currentTime past the last range end, or an 'ended' event from track transitions/ads) hit the `!range → finalize` or `ended → finalize` branch instantly → teardown in <1s.
solution: Seed state fields the UI reads (capturedMs: 0) when constructing the session object, before mount. Reuse the same video finder the overlay uses (findLargestPlayableVideo) with the old heuristic as fallback only. Add a bounded re-anchor: when the position sits past the last range OR video.ended fires while nothing has been captured, seek back to ranges[0] (max 2 attempts) instead of finalizing; only finalize after capture has happened or re-anchors are exhausted. Gate the recovery play() on !pausedByUser so an intentional pause stays paused.
principle: Boundary-state branches (past-end, ended) that finalize 'because nothing is left' are wrong when the session may legitimately start there — starting a recording is a user intent to capture the ranges, not a statement about current position. Re-anchor first, finalize only when re-anchoring failed. And any state read during flushSync/first render must exist at mount time — populate the object literal, don't fill it after.
